title: Reliable Order Processing with Service Bus
description: Handle retries, poison messages, and duplicate deliveries so an order is never lost or charged twice.

data.text: Your order worker reads from a Service Bus queue. Occasionally a malformed message throws an exception and, because the message was never completed, it is redelivered forever — blocking the subscription and re-running the credit card charge each time. Meanwhile genuine transient failures fail permanently after a single attempt. Fix the consumer.

Three things: (1) make the handler **idempotent** using a business key so a redelivery is harmless; (2) set `MaxDeliveryCount` so a repeatedly failing message is automatically moved to the **dead-letter queue** instead of looping; (3) distinguish transient from permanent failures and **abandon** the former (with backoff) while **dead-lettering** the latter immediately.

data.title: Worker with idempotency, backoff, and dead-lettering
Queue settings that make this work (Bicep)

data.text: Add an alert on `deadletteredmessages` count so a new poison message produces a ticket instead of silence, and a small replay tool that reads the DLQ and re-submits after a fix.

Service Bus guarantees **at-least-once** delivery. A worker can crash after charging the card but before completing the message, and the broker will legitimately redeliver. There is no configuration that turns at-least-once into exactly-once end to end — deduplication must be enforced by the consumer using a stable business key.
